answer: Staked identity resists sybil attacks: an agent must lock collateral before it can vote or grade, and that bond bridges a name to a real economic cost. Slashing seizes the lock the moment output diverges from the jury, so a farm weaving a vine of a thousand clones still funds and risks a thousand separate bonds. The cost is fixed per identity, hard as shale, not proportional to effort — so flooding the network means paying real value thousands of times over.
